evidence_quotes.page: PMC PMC10043969 - Affordability and basic needs: water and sanitation
evidence_quotes.quote: All Brazilian States studied in this research implemented the policy of compelling water utilities to waive payments by social tariff customers during the pandemic, which applies to low-income families with low water consumption (usually up to 10 m3/month), usually registered under the social tariff program.

Although regulatory responses prohibiting tariff increases were aimed at general users, the cut-off banning and postponement or cancelation of tariffs were strictly directed to affirmative policy users in all Brazilian states studied.

evidence_quotes.page: PMC PMC10043969 - Data collection and processing
evidence_quotes.quote: We extracted all official documents from the 25 Brazilian States' regulatory agencies’ websites published during the first 40 epidemiological weeks of 2020, comprising 634 documents.

In order to answer the research question – how are the HRtWS normative content and principles reflected in the Brazilian States' regulatory responses to the Covid-19 pandemic? – this paper provides an overview of the regulatory responses at the state level to Covid-19 from the regulatory authorities of the Brazilian states during the first epidemiological weeks of 2020.

A natural progression of this work would be to analyze the institutionalization and operationalization of the HRtWS by Brazilian regulatory authorities regarding the post-pandemic state and assess the impacts of the regulatory responses during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.

criterion_notes.c1: Topically examines regulation of water supply and sanitation service access during the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil, including regulatory provisions on service continuity, tariff waivers, disconnection bans, free reconnections, and omission of unpiped informal settlements.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Plain reading: examines state-level water and sanitation regulatory agencies' emergency resolutions and norms. Narrow rule-type reading: directly examines rule-type mechanisms governing service access, including tariff postponement/cancellation rules, prohibition of tariff increases, disconnection bans (cut-off banning), free reconnection rules, and eligibility screening rules restricting social-tariff waivers and cut-off bans to households registered in CadÚnico with water consumption up to 10 m3/month. Criterion 2 is met under both readings and does not drive exclusion.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical documentary evidence using systematic content analysis (Bardin, 2016) of 634 official documents extracted from 25 Brazilian state regulatory agencies' websites (screened to 100 pandemic-related documents and 36 utility-regulating documents yielding 75 valid regulatory responses), coded in ATLAS.ti with intercoder validation (Krippendorff's alpha > 0.5) and analyzed with co-occurrence and Pearson chi-square tests in SPSS.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: the reported outcomes are purely documentary/textual measures of regulatory responsiveness—specifically, counts of regulatory response types and textual co-occurrences/correlations with Human Rights to Water and Sanitation (HRtWS) principles, normative criteria, and named target groups within regulatory resolutions. The paper reports no empirical outcome on actual household or community water/sanitation access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, affordability, disconnections, or realized exclusion, and explicitly states in the Conclusion that assessing the impacts of the regulatory responses remains for future work.
criterion_notes.c5: The study's unit of analysis and sample (36 utility-regulating official documents yielding 75 regulatory responses from 25 Brazilian state regulatory agencies), categorization/exposure (COVID-19 state regulatory response categories), measured outcome (textual presence and co-occurrence of HRtWS principles, normative criteria, and target groups in regulatory texts), and study design (documental content analysis with cross-tabulation) are clearly identifiable, though an empirical service-access outcome is not measured.
criterion_notes.c6: Published in English, which is eligible without translation.

study_design: Documental content analysis (qualitative coding and quantitative frequency, co-occurrence, and Pearson chi-square cross-tabulation analysis of official regulatory documents)
population_and_sample: 25 Brazilian States' water and sanitation regulatory agencies; 634 official documents published during the first 40 epidemiological weeks of 2020, screened to 100 pandemic-related documents and 36 utility-regulation documents containing 75 valid regulatory responses (unit of analysis: regulatory document / regulatory response)
exposure: COVID-19 pandemic emergency and state-level water and sanitation regulatory response categories (continuity/security, affordability/tariff waivers/cut-off bans/CadÚnico targeting, and provider financial support)
outcome: Textual frequency, co-occurrence (C-values), and chi-square correlations of HRtWS principles, normative criteria, and target-group mentions within official state regulatory documents (no household or utility service-access outcome measured)
rationale: Excluded under E04 (Wrong outcome). While the paper examines rule-type water and sanitation regulatory mechanisms in Brazil during COVID-19 (tariff postponement/cancellation, prohibition of tariff increases, disconnection bans, free reconnections, and CadÚnico social-tariff eligibility rules) using systematic documental content analysis of 36 official regulatory documents (75 regulatory responses) across 25 state agencies, its measured outcome is solely the textual reflection and co-occurrence of HRtWS principles and normative criteria within the regulatory documents themselves. It does not report any empirical data (quantitative or qualitative) on actual household, community, or utility water/sanitation access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, affordability, disconnection, or exclusion outcomes, and the authors explicitly note that assessing the impacts of these regulatory responses is left for future research. Both narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings yield exclude due to failure of Criterion 4.
